headline: The number of working industrial robots worldwide passed five million, with China installing more than half of the new ones.
score_reason: Authoritative industry statistics with clear shifts in national rankings; they cover 2025.
importance_line: Factory workers and manufacturers in every major economy are affected, and the report is annual data on 2025, not a new event.
source: The Express Tribune, citing the International Federation of Robotics
summary: The Express Tribune reports figures from the International Federation of Robotics (IFR), the industry body, showing that the world's working industrial robots passed 5 million in 2025, up 9%, with annual installations up 11% to more than 600,000. China installed 354,000 units, 59% of the total, while the United States, at 38,500 installations, overtook Japan, at 36,219, to take second place; the IFR forecasts 655,000 installations this year.
notes: Figures are IFR's; the Tribune article relays them. Report release date not stated.
